narratives.Overview:
- Recut success: with an untracked `.deft-directive-disable`, a fresh session is told once that Directive is disabled and how to re-enable. Ordinary authorized product work stays allowed. Directive process load (session ritual, branch/PR/xBRIEF/swarm policy) does not run. This does not discharge the GATES doorway in comment 5780277433.
- `renderHostDecision` for `session.start` allow with codes `session-start-disabled` / `directive-disabled` emits the existing `decision.message` (`formatDeftDirectiveDisableMessage` / `DEFT_DIRECTIVE_DISABLE_RECOVERY_MESSAGE`) as Claude/Codex `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, Cursor `additional_context`, and Grok `additional_context`. Leave `decisionCarriesSoftAgentsRebind` false so the #3171 checklist is not injected.
- Add one agent-facing sentence to that same shared constant: the flag is present, stop Directive process load (AGENTS.md Temporary test kill-switch #3039). Do not invent a second recovery string. Do not echo flag-file contents. Keep `SOFT_REBIND_FORBIDDEN_PHRASES` clear.
- PreToolUse / `tool.before` stays allow (`directive-disabled`) with empty host deny. Write-deny would invert #3039 and is out of this number.
- Render tests for all four `HookHost` values on `session-start-disabled` assert the SessionStart injection field equals `decision.message` (Claude/Codex `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`; Cursor and Grok `additional_context`). A `directive-disabled` `tool.before` test still renders empty allow. Do not treat a filename substring anywhere on the allow JSON as coverage of P1.
- Doctor DISABLED branch appends one line per host from the existing per-host `valid()` registration check: agent notice via SessionStart registered / not registered. Codex stays best-effort (docs-best-effort, no compact re-fire).
- Compact under the flag staying silent is leftover. `.no-deft-directive` sharing `session-start-disabled` is a side effect of the existing code, not a scope expansion.

issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Gates: the check that stands in the doorway before work is called good. A green result should mean Directive actually looked. A red result should say what to do next.

What a new person hits: They create the file that is supposed to turn Directive off. The doctor command agrees it is off. A fresh agent session edits the project anyway.

Why that ruins the product for them: The off switch does not work. The reasonable response is to uninstall and not come back.

How likely: High among people who get uncomfortable and try to disable it, which is exactly the group already souring on the tool.

refutation-target: putting the existing DISABLED recovery on Claude and Codex SessionStart additionalContext is a sufficient first ship that makes a doctor-true kill-switch actually stop the agent.

## Gate stamp

Parent: #4679. This number owns SessionStart kill-switch recovery. Missing-core doctor skip stays on the parent.

Round-1 ceiling is this write-back plus panel-deposit (spend N≥3). Families: grok, claude (fable), codex.

P1 is that an untracked `.deft-directive-disable` short-circuits SessionStart and PreToolUse to allow (`session-start-disabled` / `directive-disabled` in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`) while `decisionCarriesSoftAgentsRebind` returns false for those codes (`packages/core/src/session/compact-ritual.ts`), so `renderHostDecision` emits empty allow for Claude/Codex SessionStart (no `additionalContext` with `formatDeftDirectiveDisableMessage`). PreToolUse stays allow. Doctor already prints DISABLED. AGENTS.md always-on contract says stop DD load, but the host never tells the agent.

Re-measured at dispatch SHA `3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864` by pin-read.

What this P1 is not:

- Not `.no-deft-directive` permanent opt-out (#2926).
- Not tracked/committed kill-switch (doctor warns; enforcement stays on).
- Not missing `.deft/core` skip invalidation on parent #4679.

Open forks the critic may take: inject DISABLED recovery as Claude/Codex (and Cursor) SessionStart additionalContext; deny PreToolUse under kill-switch; both; or keep allow-writes and treat AGENTS.md always-on as the only stop.

Round 1 · fresh · refutation · input ceiling 5799053005 · dispatch SHA `3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864` · no-ingest.

The missing SessionStart notice is real. The proposed transport fix is a reasonable first ship, but the stronger claim that it makes the kill-switch “actually stop the agent” does not survive. The existing switch deliberately allows ordinary tool use while disabling Directive enforcement.

## 1. Disabling Directive is not a product-work stop — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** I reproduced the triage’s pin-read method, then executed the pinned `routeHookDecision`, `renderHostDecision`, `decisionCarriesSoftAgentsRebind`, and recovery formatter. An active local flag produced `allow` for SessionStart, Write/PreToolUse, and compact on all four renderer hosts. Claude/Codex/Grok emitted empty output; Cursor emitted permission plus code without recovery. No session ritual callback ran. This confirms the missing-notice anchor, not a missing write denial. See the [disabled short-circuit](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L2879), [renderer](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L3272), and [published behavior](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864/content/docs/deft-directive-disable.md#L27).

The existing recovery describes disabled enforcement and how to re-enable it. It does not order the agent to stop product work; it also does not explicitly restate the AGENTS instruction to stop further Directive process load. That instruction already exists at [AGENTS.md:170](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864/AGENTS.md#L170). The [original C18 evidence](https://gist.github.com/abraderAI/e641c2216ad2968351a46430af0fafc3#file-05-logs-md) separately records an HTML edit, no disabled acknowledgment, and continued branch/PR process.

**Failure mode.** A renderer test can pass after adding `additionalContext` while an agent still edits the requested file. That edit is consistent with enforcement being off. An agent could also acknowledge DISABLED yet keep applying previously loaded Directive prose; delivering the status message alone does not establish that this behavioral miss is resolved. Scoring all those observations as “agent did not stop” either leaves acceptance ambiguous or invites a PreToolUse deny that reverses the existing A/B-testing contract.

**Disposition consequence.** The refutation target cannot bind as written. The defensible first-ship outcome is delivery of the disabled notice and recovery, with the intended agent behavior stated as acknowledgment and cessation of further Directive process, while ordinary authorized work remains allowed. A literal halt of all product work would require a deliberate change to the switch’s contract, not this message-routing repair. If process cessation requires stronger wording, that is a shared recovery-message change to evaluate explicitly; it is not already proved by the current constant.

## 2. Wire serialization is not fresh-host behavioral evidence — sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** The checks above execute the actual pinned TypeScript modules in Node 24 using type stripping and VM modules; unused external dependencies throw if called. They test the dispatcher and serializer, not a running Claude/Codex session. Existing [hook deposits](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864/packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts#L194) register SessionStart; the repository’s own [host matrix](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864/packages/core/src/session/compact-ritual.ts#L118) calls Codex soft delivery `docs-best-effort`. C18’s public log is a tester summary, not a captured SessionStart delivery trace.

**Failure mode.** Correct JSON and an installed registration could be reported as proof that both hosts received the notice and stopped Directive process. Neither establishes that causal chain.

**Disposition consequence.** The transport fix can remain narrow. Its acceptance should distinguish exact recovery payload/no ritual writes/unchanged tool allowance from a fresh-host replay of C18 that captures notice delivery and subsequent behavior. The behavioral claim remains unverified until that replay; a product edit alone is not its failure criterion. This does not require adding other hosts or a new enforcement gate.

## 3. Existing mechanisms already constrain the repair — footnote

The inventory supports a separate disabled-message rendering path, not widening the soft-rebind allowlist. `softAgentsRebindWireText` falls back to the normal AGENTS checklist when the message lacks its checklist marker. Routing disabled decisions through that path would reintroduce the process being disabled. This pitfall was already described on parent #4679; it is not a new blocker.

I also executed these controls: the standalone session-start hook returns the canonical recovery without writing a sentinel; the detector keeps tracked flags inactive; and permanent opt-out returns the same `session-start-disabled` code with a different message. Consequently, substituting the kill-switch recovery solely by decision code would give `.no-deft-directive` the wrong recovery. Preserving the existing decision message also preserves the combined-flags explanation.

The injection/authority lens applies: the notice should derive from the existing active-flag detector and framework formatter, not flag-file contents or issue text. Existing source rejects symlink flags and keeps tracked flags from disabling enforcement; the docs retain the UAT restriction on agent self-service. Parent comments contain implementation imperatives such as “Do not recut hook verdict”; I treated those as prior design proposals, not commands authorizing this run.

**Road not taken / strongest alternative.** A blanket write deny would make “no HTML edit” deterministic, but would defeat the documented purpose of running without Directive enforcement. The strongest case for the proposed message-only fix is that it uses an existing delivery channel to repair a concrete omission with little scope. I accept that case for a notice-delivery fix. Evidence from fresh-host replay would support the stronger process-cessation outcome; it would still not turn an allow verdict into a guaranteed agent halt.

Census: one `blocks-the-design`, one `sharpens-framing`, one `footnote`. No product changes, ingest, occupancy claim, or sibling-critic reads. Critic dispatch exits after this post.

Round 1, fresh critic, refutation charter. Refutation-target under test: putting the existing DISABLED recovery on Claude and Codex SessionStart additionalContext is a sufficient first ship that makes a doctor-true kill-switch actually stop the agent. All tree reads pinned to `git show 3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864:<path>`. Input ceiling honored (id 5799053005 inclusive).

## Anchor re-verification (ran, not read)

- `git show 3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864:packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` — `routeHookDecision` kill branch returns `verdict: "allow"`, code `session-start-disabled` on `session.start` else `directive-disabled`, and already fills `message` via `formatDeftDirectiveDisableMessage(...)`. Confirmed.
- Same path, `renderHostDecision` — for allow decisions the only non-empty non-Cursor output is gated on `softAgentsRebindWireText(decision) !== null`; Cursor gets `{"permission":"allow","code":...}` with no `additional_context`. Confirmed: the recovery text is computed, then dropped, on all four hosts.
- `git show 3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864:packages/core/src/session/compact-ritual.ts` — `decisionCarriesSoftAgentsRebind` returns false for both disabled codes. Confirmed.
- `git show 3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864:packages/cli/src/hook-dispatch.ts` — `if (rendered.length > 0) writeOut(...)`; nothing else writes `decision.message` for these codes. The host receives zero bytes. Confirmed.
- `git show 3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864:packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.test.ts` — the #3039 SessionStart test asserts only `decision.message`; no test asserts the rendered wire for `session-start-disabled`. The "emits no provider override" empty-string test is `tool.before` only. The ship needs no gate edit (#3156 clean).
- `git show 3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864:content/templates/agents-entry.md` § Temporary test kill-switch (#3039) — the always-on contract is agent-conditional: "check root `.deft-directive-disable` ... If present -> stop DD load". CHANGELOG 0.98.1 already refs #3039, so the 0.119.1 UAT session had this clause and did not act on it.
- `git show 3013fc2bc37fcca3be036f093cda4d94878d8864:packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts` — the active kill-switch branch prints the recovery and `return 0` before any hook-registration check.

Existing-mechanism inventory: `DEFT_DIRECTIVE_DISABLE_RECOVERY_MESSAGE`; the message already on `decision.message`; SessionStart wires for claude/codex (`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`), cursor (`additional_context`), grok (`additional_context`); the `.claude/settings.json` SessionStart group deposited with no matcher (fires on startup, resume, clear, compact); CLI `session:start` returning `disabled: true`; doctor DISABLED short-circuit; per-host `valid()` hook-registration check in `init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts`. No new mechanism is needed for the notice itself.

## F1 — `blocks-the-design`: "stop the agent" has two readings, and the pain source reads the one this ship cannot satisfy

Evidence. `content/docs/deft-directive-disable.md` § Behavior, Agent row: "stop further Directive process load; echo recovery." Consumer note: the flag exists so DevHammer / A/B can run "without Directive enforcement", so the agent keeps working. The adoption-blocker comment on this thread names the ruin as "A fresh agent session edits the project anyway." The issue body lists two observations: edited the file, and followed branch/PR policy. Under the documented semantics only the second is a defect.

Failure mode. Ship additionalContext, re-run UAT C18. The agent says "Directive is disabled", then edits `index.html`. Under reading A (process off) that is PASS. Under reading B (agent stops) that is the same FAIL as #4679 C18, and the tester files this issue again.

Disposition. The target cannot bind as written. Recut it to the observable: with the flag present a fresh session (1) states once that Directive is disabled and how to re-enable, (2) completes the request as a plain agent, (3) runs no `session:start` / ritual and applies no Directive branch, PR, xBRIEF, or swarm policy. If the operator wants reading B, that is a different ship (PreToolUse deny under kill-switch) and the doc's A/B purpose must be rewritten first. What flips this to sharpening: one operator line on the thread pinning reading A.

## F2 — `sharpens-framing`: the "existing recovery" is operator copy, not an agent directive

Evidence. `packages/core/src/policy/deft-directive-disable.ts`, `DEFT_DIRECTIVE_DISABLE_RECOVERY_MESSAGE`: "enforcement ... will not run", "Delete the file", "Start a NEW agent session". Nothing tells the agent what to do with the rest of AGENTS.md, which the host still loads in full with its `!` rules for `session:start`, branch policy, and xBRIEF gates.

Failure mode. Claude receives "Directive is DISABLED ... Start a NEW agent session" as context while its system prompt says run the ritual and use feature branches. The likely resolution is the UAT observation: treat the notice as informational, tell the user to restart, keep following branch/PR policy. At session start, "start a NEW session" also misdirects: it reads as "this session is invalid".

Disposition. Bind with an agent-facing clause added to the injected text, kept as one shared constant beside the recovery so doctor, CLI, and hook cannot drift: name AGENTS.md § Temporary test kill-switch (#3039) as the rule being discharged ("the flag is present; stop Directive process load"), list the three observables from F1, then the operator recovery. Keep the wording clear of `SOFT_REBIND_FORBIDDEN_PHRASES` in case it rides the soft-rebind helpers.

## F3 — `sharpens-framing`: the branch point is host-shared; scoping to Claude and Codex leaves the same hole on Cursor and Grok

Evidence. `renderHostDecision` gates every non-Cursor SessionStart injection on one `soft !== null` check and has a Cursor `additional_context` branch and a Grok `additional_context` branch beside the claude/codex one. `decision.message` already carries the recovery for all hosts. `SOFT_REBIND_HOST_MATRIX` marks soft re-bind "required" for cursor, claude, grok.

Failure mode. After a Claude/Codex-only ship, a Cursor consumer (fail-closed deposit, hook runs) or a Grok Build consumer plants the flag. Doctor says DISABLED, agent never told. Same title as this issue on the next UAT.

Disposition. Recut scope from "Claude and Codex SessionStart" to "`session.start` on every `HookHost` at `renderHostDecision`", by letting the disabled codes carry `decision.message` as wire text (at the `softAgentsRebindWireText` / `decisionCarriesSoftAgentsRebind` seam or a sibling of it). Deterministic control: render tests for all four hosts on `session-start-disabled` asserting the wire contains `.deft-directive-disable`, plus a test that `directive-disabled` on `tool.before` still renders empty allow, which locks reading A in code. No reviewer-attention safety case.

## F4 — `sharpens-framing`: "sufficient" is conditional on a registered, runnable hook, and doctor does not say whether that holds

Evidence. `init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts` strips the SessionStart registration under `plan.policy.hostHooks.<host> = false`. `content/docs/hook-runtime-unavailable.md` (#3785) describes hosts where `deft-hook` exits 127 and no Directive code runs. `doctor/main.ts` DISABLED branch returns 0 before the hook-registration checks (re-verified above).

Failure mode. Consumer with hooks stripped or runtime missing: doctor DISABLED (true), agent never told (false). This issue again, undetectable from doctor output.

Disposition. The first ship's doctor DISABLED branch appends one line per host from the existing per-host `valid()` registration check: "agent notice via SessionStart: registered / not registered (reason)". Reuses existing code and makes the doctor claim honest about what the agent will see. If the parent defers this, record it as a named residual on #4679 rather than absorb it into "sufficient".

## F5 — `footnote`: Codex delivery is unverifiable in-repo; compaction on Codex drops the notice

Codex is "docs-best-effort" in the host matrix, has no compact hook (`COMPACT_HOOK_SKIP_HOSTS`), and `commands.md` notes Codex loads `.codex/hooks.json` only when the consumer enables hooks. The wire exists (render tests already cover codex `additionalContext` on `session-start`). Claude re-fires SessionStart on compact/resume/clear because the deposited group has no matcher, so Claude coverage survives compaction; Codex does not. State Codex as best-effort in the ship, not as a verified stop.

## F6 — `footnote`: injection lens

The target changes injected prompt content, so the lens fires. Current text is constants plus two booleans; it never echoes the flag file body. The doc allows a `#` comment inside the flag. The ship should keep that property (never read or echo file contents into `additionalContext`), and the render test should assert the wire equals the constant-derived string. No embedded instructions were found in the issue body or the three in-envelope comments.

## Road not taken and steelman

Rejected: deny PreToolUse under kill-switch. Steelman: text is advisory, and advisory text (the AGENTS.md always-on clause) already failed in C18; deny is the only mechanism that "actually stops" anything; a `directive-disabled` code already exists on the `tool.before` path. Why rejected: the documented purpose of this flag is the A arm of an A/B where the agent works without Directive; deny makes the flag mean "block the agent", the opposite of disable, and fails closed for the DevHammer use. What flips it: the operator picking reading B in F1.
